insights.concise_text: Pre-ordering English sentences with the CFILT-preorder system to match Indian language word order significantly improves BLEU scores over baseline scores in X-Hindi experiments.

triple.subject: CFILT-preorder system
triple.object: baseline BLEU scores

insights.concise_text: Because English is the assisting source language and all primary source languages have canonical SOV word order, the proposed SVO-to-SOV pre-ordering targets English-Hindi parent training.

triple.subject: SVO-to-SOV pre-ordering
triple.object: English-Hindi parent task

insights.concise_text: The extremely low-resource setting with no parallel corpus for the child task is addressed by word-by-word translation into English using a bilingual dictionary before parent-model translation.

triple.subject: no parallel corpus for the child task
triple.object: word-by-word translation into English using a bilingual dictionary

insights.concise_text: The contextual representation being word-order dependent explains why SVO English and SOV source languages create inconsistent encoder representations that limit transfer learning benefits.

triple.subject: word-order dependent contextual representation
triple.object: inconsistent encoder representations that limit transfer learning benefits

insights.concise_text: The BLEU score improvements from both pre-ordering configurations provide evidence for the conclusion that pre-ordering the assisting language significantly improves translation quality in an extremely low-resource setting.

triple.subject: BLEU score improvements
triple.object: pre-ordering the assisting language significantly improves translation quality

insights.concise_text: Generic pre-ordering rules, which apply to all Indian languages, produced larger BLEU gains than Hindi-tuned rules in X-Hindi experiments.

triple.subject: generic pre-ordering rules
triple.object: Hindi-tuned pre-ordering rules on BLEU gains

insights.concise_text: The proposed pre-ordering of English sentences to match source-language word order addresses the previously unexplored effect of word order divergence in transfer learning for multilingual NMT.

triple.subject: pre-ordering English sentences
triple.object: word order divergence in transfer learning for multilingual NMT

insights.concise_text: The standard sequence-to-sequence architecture with attention used in experiments makes the word-order-dependent encoder contextual representations relevant to the proposed pre-ordering solution.

triple.subject: standard sequence-to-sequence architecture with attention
triple.object: consistent word-order-dependent encoder contextual representations

insights.concise_text: The finding that pre-ordered models generate fewer UNK tokens supports the BLEU score improvements observed for both pre-ordering configurations.

triple.subject: fewer UNK tokens
triple.object: BLEU score improvements from pre-ordering configurations

insights.concise_text: The current work focused on Indian languages, so the proposed benefit of pre-ordering for other word order divergence scenarios such as SOV to SVO remains unverified.

triple.subject: focus on Indian languages
triple.object: verification of SOV to SVO pre-ordering benefit
